text:
Sam: Quick update from the warmers comparison run (2 days): deploy-time prefill vs autoscale-triggered prefill vs scheduled synthetic. Wanted to surface hit-rate, tail behavior, and a couple regressions.
Mia: Can you share the headline numbers?
Sam: Headline: deploy-prefill hits KV prefix hit-rate much faster (median 45% -> 82% within ~5m after deploy), but we saw transient p95 latency spikes (1.8x) on hosts that had mixed-model workloads. Autoscale-prefill ramps slower to ~70% in 10m but much smoother tail. Scheduled synthetic (current nightly) gives ~60% after 30m, but quality of hits poorer.
Donna: Important: what's the cache keying scheme in the experiment? Full prompt+meta or prefix-only?
Sam: We tested two key schemes. Current experiment used prefix-normalized scheme. Example we used:```
// pseudo
key = sha256(normalize(prefix) + "|" + model_id + "|" + quant_profile)
```
But one run accidentally included sampling params for a subset which exploded cardinality.
Anita: Bingo — we found after PR #4213 the batching heuristic changed to favor micro-batches for very short sequences. That caused different kernel selection paths (kernel A vs kernel B) and a small per-token regression (~6-8ms/token) that amplified when combined with cache thrash.
Tony: I uploaded flame graphs and kernel-switch traces here: https://internal.redwood/perf/1825-prefill-graphs (see host 7f2c for kernel churn).
Lee: Observed mismatch between synthetic and real traffic. Our synthetic generator used short single-turn prompts; real traffic has longer multi-sentence prefixes. Short synthetic -> different KV hit semantics and better apparent hit-rates but lower user-observed quality. We should stratify synthetic by prefix length and prompt templates.
infra-bot: Scheduled job created: `prefill-orch-182501` -> runs 30m prefill at deploy for prod2 on canaries.
deploy-bot: Canary run started: warmer tasks enqueued 5k synthetic requests over 10m window.
Mia: Also saw weird eviction patterns: when prefill floods a host with many similar hashed keys, we get collisions and early evictions; p99 latency spikes. Need to revisit eviction policy and per-host TTL heuristics.
Sam: Agreed. Proposed action items:
  1) Switch warmers to stratified synthetic (length, template diversity) — owners: Mia/Lee
  2) Normalize cache keys to drop non-deterministic runtime params (temp, seed) — owner: Donna/Anita
  3) Prevent batching heuristic toggles during prefill window (prefer stable kernel) — owner: Eng-runtime (Anita)
  4) Add metrics: kernel-switch-count, prefill-eviction-rate, per-host cache-warmth (fraction of requests hitting prefills) — owner: Sam
Donna: I'll open the PR for key normalization and add a migration test for cardinality.
Anita: I'll run a small regression matrix across seq-len distribution and quant profiles to catch kernel-selection jitter.
Sam: Note on model variants: when prefill targets a model variant different from what runtime will pick under load (eg heavier quantized variant), we saw quality mismatches. Warmers must pick the same variant selection policy as runtime routing.
Lee: For stratified synthetic, I'll prepare a short script that replays representative prefixes from the last 24h (anonymized) and generates a distribution file we can feed to warmers.
Mia: Also let's add a canary gate: reject deploy if prefill warms > X eviction_rate or kernel-switch-count spikes > Y in first 10m.
Tony: I'll add instrumentation links to the runbook and the perf dashboards.
Sam: Cool. Summary: deploy-prefill = faster hit-rate but riskier on tail without key normalization and batching stability; autoscale-prefill = safer tail but slower ramp; stratified synthetic seems best compromise for scheduled jobs.
Sam: Action owners + timeline? Can we get PRs and test runs this week?
Mia: +1, will start on stratified generator today.
Donna: PR in progress, target EOD for review.
Anita: Regression matrix scheduled tomorrow morning.
Sam: Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
